text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- A new emergency exercise in the tunnel section of the Great Belt fixed link between Denmark's two biggest islands is to be conducted in April, but no organiser been found yet. The organiser of the first unsuccessful safety drill last month, the Great Belt Link Company, does not want to take responsibility for a new drill, after heavy criticism. The road-rail, tunnel-bridge fixed link across the Great Belt opens this summer.

--- Telecoms group Tele Danmark employees are much more efficient than competitors in the Danish market with Tele Danmark earnings per employee four times higher than its main rival Swedish Telia, a survey shows.
--- Denmark's Shareholders Association accuses large Danish banks and dealers of manipulating prices on options and futures on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange.
--- Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) is flying an increasing number of customers on free holidays through its ticket bonus system with 175,000 Scandinavians saving bonus points for free holidays in 1996.

--- At a Nordic Council conference in Copenhagen prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said that he accepted the idea of an European Union in which countries like France and Germany could have closer cooperation in certain areas than partner member states, changing his previous stance against a twin- track EU.
